title: Naomi Watts to Be Honored at San Sebastián Film Festival
description:
British star Naomi Watts will receive the San Sebastián Film Festival’s prestigious Donostia Award during its 74th edition in September. 

	She join
body:
British star Naomi Watts will receive the San Sebastián Film Festival’s prestigious Donostia Award during its 74th edition in September. 

	She joins legendary German director Werner Herzog whose Donostia Award was announced early August.

	Watts will pick up her Award on Saturday, Sept. 19 and screen “The Housewife, the directorial debut of Canadian Ben Shirinian.” 


	“Watts combines independent films with big productions on both the big and the small screen,” the San Sebastián Film Festival said in a statement, calling her “one of her generation’s most talented and award-winning actresses.”
	

	Born in England, but achieving a career in the U.S. and beyond, Watts broke out in David Lynch’s “Mullholland Drive,” where her performance is “ranked among the finest in contemporary cinema,” said the San Sebastián Festival.

	She scored Academy Award nominations for best actress for Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s “21 Grams,” and an Academy Award nomination for J.A. Bayona’s “The Impossible.”

	Watts has also worked with Peter Jackson, David Cronenberg, Clint Eastwood, Michael Haneke, Audrey Diwan, Noah Baumbach and Rodrigo García, with whom she came to San Sebastián in 2009 to close the Official Selection out of competition with “Mother & Child.”

	She earned a first Emmy Award nomination for her portrayal of Babe Paley in Ryan Murphy’s “Feud: Capote vs. The Swans.”

	Many of her roles play off Watts’ demure appearance to reveal depths of desire and envy (“Mulholland Drive”) or unexpected courage (“The Impossible”) in a career which has paid tribute to the multiplicity of human potential, and characters’ complexity.
	

	“The Housewife,” the Donostia Award Screening, stars Watts, Tye Sheridan, Luke Evans, Michael Imperioli and Lena Olin. Set in 1964 and based on a true story, the film tells the tale of a young journalist who tracks down a potential Nazi officer living secretly in New York and befriends the suspect’s charming wife.

	The San Sebastián Film Festival runs Sept. 18 to 26.

schema.headline: Naomi Watts to Be Honored at San Sebastián Film Festival

title: DraftKings Taps Kevin Hart, Nick Jonas for Road-Trip Commercial That Touts Wagering, Predictions
description:
Nick Jonas has been on plenty of road trips — but none quite like this.

	The actor and musician plays a prominent role in what is expected to be a
body:
Nick Jonas has been on plenty of road trips — but none quite like this.

	The actor and musician plays a prominent role in what is expected to be a significant and long-running campaign for sports-wagering giant DraftKings. In a new ad, Jonas and comedian Kevin Hart appear to take a massive road trip, visiting many different parts of the country. And while Jonas is no stranger to traversing the nation, often on a tour bus, he may not have been accustomed to the way it was done on the commercial’s set.
	

	“When you’re shooting like that, the vehicle that you’re in is on a practical trailer. It can’t be on. Therefore, the air conditioning can’t be on at all,” Jonas recalls, even though he and Hart felt they were working during “one of the hottest days in New York, New Jersey, of the year.”


	“We were both kind of kind of dying in the car, and the windows had to be rolled all the way up for it to look the right way for the camera shot,” Jonas recalls. “But we survived.”



	And now, the payoff. Fans of NFL and the NBA are likely to see the commercial in various iterations for weeks.  The campaign will continue throughout the football and basketball seasons, and DraftKings will also run additional creative featuring Chad Ochocinco and Carmelo Anthony. In addition to the national advertising, DraftKings expects to make promotional forays into local markets as well.

	With sports wagering gaining approval in the bulk of the nation, except for 11 states including California, Texas, Georgia and Minnesota, companies like DraftKings and rivals such as FanDuel and BetMGM continue to move aggressively to court sports fans. Football aficionados are likely to encounter the DraftKings pitch week after week, so Jonas and Hart need to demonstrate winning chemistry.
	

	Sports fans by this time expect to hear a lot from DraftKings during game time. The company spent approximately $69.5 million to advertise during NFL games in 2025, according to data from iSpot, a tracker of ad spending, and approximately $12.8 million to run commercials during NBA games last year. Some of the company’s most likable commercials in the past have relied on celebrities, according to iSpot, including Hart.

	The goal of the ad effort is to help consumers understand that they can interact with DraftKings across the U.S., says Stephane Sherman, DraftKings’ chief marketing officer, during a recent interview. Thanks to the rise of prediction markets, DraftKings now offers services throughout the nation, not just in states that allow sports wagering.

	“It is a real change for us from a business standpoint,” she says. The campaign will “invite more fans to be a part of the DraftKings experience.”

	Entertainment fans have seen Jonas and Hart work together before, in two of the recent “Jumanji” movies. But the bet (no pun intended) here is that the push-and-pull of Hart, who often comes across with high energy and Jonas, who plays more of a straight man, will get audiences to focus more intently.

	“We were trying to boil the ocean a little bit,” acknowledges Chaucer Barnes, chief marketing officer of Translation, the marketing agency that helped devise the commercials. DraftKings wants consumers to understand that the company now offers a broader array of services. “We need you to lean in because we actually have big news to deliver,” he says.

	The hope is the actors keep things cool on screen, even if they navigated a little warmth behind the scenes.

schema.headline: DraftKings Taps Kevin Hart, Nick Jonas for Road-Trip Commercial That Touts Wagering, Predictions

title: Korea Box Office: ‘The Odyssey’ Eclipses ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’
description:
“The Odyssey” held onto the top spot at the South Korean box office during the weekend of Aug. 28–30. 

	According to data from KOBIS, the tracking
body:
“The Odyssey” held onto the top spot at the South Korean box office during the weekend of Aug. 28–30. 

	According to data from KOBIS, the tracking service operated by the Korean Film Council, the Christopher Nolan-directed tentpole generated $8.7 million from 1,058,642 admissions over the three-day frame across 2,071 screens, capturing 64.7% of total weekend business. Continuing its powerhouse late-summer theatrical run in its fourth weekend of release, the film lifted its cumulative South Korean gross to $71.7 million from 8,864,947 total admissions since its Aug. 5 launch.
	

	Superhero blockbuster “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” remained in second place during its fifth weekend, pulling in $1.9 million from 250,442 admissions over the frame. The film accounted for 14.4% of the weekend market, pushing its cumulative local haul to $65 million from 8,548,400 admissions.


	Local family road-trip drama “The Journey to Gyeongju” debuted in third place, generating $912,660 from 124,963 admissions across 801 screens. Directed by Kim Mi-jo, the narrative follows a grieving mother and her three daughters who embark on a journey to Gyeongju to confront the released perpetrator responsible for the death of their youngest family member. Starring Lee Jung-eun, Gong Hyo-jin, Park So-dam, Lee Yeon, and Byun Yo-han, the film has collected $1.3 million from 192,384 total admissions since its Aug. 26 rollout.

	“The End of Oak Street” opened in fourth place, pulling in $476,938 from 63,472 admissions over the weekend. Since its Aug. 26 arrival, the title has brought $783,473 from 107,438 admissions.
	

	Local animated film “Teenieping: Legend of the Whale Heartstone” finished in fifth place, adding $283,019 from 39,740 admissions. Directed by Kim Soo-hoon, the musical fantasy adventure follows Princess Romi, Heartsping, and their companions exploring an undersea kingdom to rescue Queen Velita. The family film has reached $5.7 million from 838,709 viewers since its Aug. 5 launch.

	“Insidious: Out of the Further” took sixth place in its sophomore outing, bringing in $169,467 from 22,129 admissions. The horror entry has lifted its overall South Korean total past the million-dollar mark to $1.1 million from 148,333 viewers.

	“Detective Conan the Movie: Fallen Angel of the Highway” landed in seventh place, collecting $154,613 from 20,686 admissions. Directed by Takahiro Hasui, the franchise installment has earned $2.9 million from 403,090 admissions.

	The local action-comedy sequel “Ok! Madam: Bon Voyage” took eighth place, generating $80,132 from 10,969 admissions. Directed by Lee Cheol-ha and starring Uhm Jung-hwa, Park Sung-woong, Lee Sang-yun, and Sooyoung, the comedy has moved its cume to $2.2 million from 334,907 ticket buyers.

	“Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie” placed ninth, taking $60,367 from 8,636 admissions over the frame to push its cume to $749,164 from 106,540 viewers.

	Rounding out the top 10 was the local animated fantasy “Ghost Band,” which opened to $42,077 from 7,961 admissions. Directed by Geum Dong-ho, the musical animation follows a singer-songwriter with the supernatural ability to see spirits who joins forces with a quartet of ghosts to form a musical troupe. Since its Aug. 26 rollout, the indie animation has grossed $71,175 from 13,803 total admissions.

	The overall market collective gross for the weekend was $13.5 million, down from last week’s $16.1 million.

schema.headline: Korea Box Office: ‘The Odyssey’ Eclipses ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’

title: China Box Office: ‘Once Upon a Time in the Middle East’ Continues Dominance
description: Dirty Monkeys’ war comedy-drama “Once Upon a Time in the Middle East” held onto the top spot at the mainland China box office for the third consecut
body:
Dirty Monkeys’ war comedy-drama “Once Upon a Time in the Middle East” held onto the top spot at the mainland China box office for the third consecutive weekend, grossing RMB174.4 million ($25.6 million) over the Aug. 28–30 frame, according to data from Artisan Gateway. 

	Directed by Wen Muye (“Dying to Survive”) and produced by Ning Hao, the summer breakout has pushed its cumulative haul to $283.7 million since its August 11 launch. Starring Shen Teng, Jiang Qiming, Aarif Rahman, and Omar Sherif, the story follows a debt-ridden Chinese chef in a fictional Middle Eastern city who transforms his restaurant into a sanctuary for local orphans and civilians after armed conflict breaks out.
	

	Pearl River Film Group’s crime drama “V” maintained second place in its sophomore weekend, generating $14.4 million to push its cumulative Chinese earnings to $59.6 million. Directed by Han Yan (“Love Never Ends”), the feature stars Tony Leung Ka Fai, Zhu Yilong, Tan Jianci, and Kara Wai in a narrative chronicling an ambitious man’s rapid rise to power and the dark fallout that threatens his success.


	Universal’s epic “The Odyssey” held third position, collecting $10 million in its third weekend. The film has amassed a cumulative gross of $87.4 million across mainland theaters. 

	Pearl Studio’s animated fantasy feature “All Wishes Come True!” placed fourth in its seventh weekend of release, taking in $7.9 million. Directed by Mu Zhengyang, the film has generated $270.3 million since its July 18 premiere.

	Sony’s superhero tentpole “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” rounded out the top five, adding $2.9 million in its fifth frame. The film has lifted its cumulative total to $225.7 million, remaining the year’s top-earning Hollywood import in China.
	

	Mainland China’s overall weekend grosses reached $69.8 million, while the 2026 year-to-date revenue stands at $4.13 billion, down 28.1% from the same period in 2025.

schema.headline: China Box Office: ‘Once Upon a Time in the Middle East’ Continues Dominance

title: Rintaro Returns to Korea After 17 Years for Busan’s Japanese Animation Special
description: The 31st Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) has unveiled a 13-film Japanese Animation Special program, marking the first Korea visit in 17 yea
body:
The 31st Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) has unveiled a 13-film Japanese Animation Special program, marking the first Korea visit in 17 years for animation master Rintaro alongside four next-generation directors.

	Billed as a Special Program in Focus, the lineup puts a spotlight on Japan’s animation history across a full century, mixing formative classics with buzzed-about new releases and one European work that shaped generations of Japanese animators. Most of the lineup has rarely played Korean theaters, and several titles will have their Korean premieres at the festival.
	

	Rintaro will travel to Busan alongside directors Kadowaki Kohei, Katanosaka Ryo, Natsume Shingo and Shinomiya Yoshitoshi, who represent the medium’s newer generation. It is Rintaro’s first trip to Korea in 17 years.


	The lineup’s classics section opens with Yabushita Taiji’s “The White Snake Enchantress” (1958), an adaptation of a Chinese folk tale about a young man who falls for a serpent capable of taking human form. It was the first Japanese animated feature made in full color, and it left a lasting impression on a teenage Miyazaki Hayao, who wrote in “Starting Point 1979-1996” that watching it left him in tears until dawn. The film stands as a landmark work from Toei Animation.

	Yamamoto Eiichi’s “Belladonna of Sadness” (1973) was produced by Mushi Production as an experimental work aimed at adult viewers. Adapted from Jules Michelet’s “La Sorcière,” the story centers on Jeanne, a woman who strikes a bargain with the Devil and emerges transformed into a witch. The film was invited to screen at the 1973 Berlin Film Festival, shortly after its debut, and it later became a global cult title following a 2016 4K restoration. Actor Nakadai Tatsuya provides the Devil’s voice, while the camera drifts across static watercolor paintings under Fukai Kuni’s art direction.
	

	“Phoenix 2772 (Space Firebird)” (1980) draws on Tezuka Osamu’s “Phoenix” manga saga, with Tezuka serving as writer and director on the project. Its 12-minute opening, which traces the protagonist’s growth using only music and imagery and no spoken dialogue, stands as one of the film’s most discussed passages.

	Oshii Mamoru’s “Angel’s Egg” (1985), made with illustrator Yoshitaka Amano, unfolds with almost no dialogue, relying instead on biblical symbolism and imagery. The film laid the groundwork for a visual approach Oshii carried forward into “Ghost in the Shell” (1995).

	“Memories” (1995), overseen by Otomo Katsuhiro of “Akira” (1988), comes back to Busan three decades after it screened at the festival’s first edition. The program will show a 2025 remaster marking the film’s 30th anniversary, presenting all three episodes of the omnibus.

	“Metropolis” (2001) draws its story from a 1949 manga by Tezuka Osamu. Rintaro, whose credits include “Galaxy Express 999” (1979), directed the film, and Otomo Katsuhiro wrote the screenplay. Production took five years, with a budget among the largest in Japanese animation history at that point.

	Yuasa Masaaki made his feature directorial debut with “Mind Game” (2004), adapting a manga of the same name by Robin Nishi. Yuasa, known for his work on “Crayon Shin-chan” and “Chibi Maruko-chan,” saw the film take the Animation Division’s Grand Prize at the 2005 Japan Media Arts Festival, plus the Mainichi Film Awards’ 2004 Ofuji Noburo Award for Animation.

	“Kakurenbo” (2004) is where Morita Shuhei made his directorial debut. He later picked up an Academy Award nomination for Best Animated Short Film for “Possessions” (2013) and went on to direct “Tokyo Ghoul” (2014). The 24-minute short built a cult following for pairing 3D CG with cel-style rendering, an unusual combination for its era.

	Four new titles round out the lineup, with all four directors attending BIFF. “Ghost – End of Night” comes from director Natsume Shingo, who also made “One-Punch Man” (2015), with production handled by Madhouse Inc. The film heads to BIFF ahead of a planned 2027 theatrical bow in Japan.

	“Shiranui” is a 36-minute theatrical short produced by CoMix Wave Films, the company known for many of Shinkai Makoto’s biggest titles. The studio found first-time filmmaker Katanosaka Ryo and backed him in making an original work for cinemas. He personally hand-drew close to two-thirds of the picture’s 325 rough cuts.
	

	Kadowaki Kohei directs “We Are Aliens,” a rotoscoped feature with a distinctly realistic look. The film played in the Directors’ Fortnight sidebar during this year’s Cannes Film Festival, and it also screened in Competition at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival.

	Director Shinomiya Yoshitoshi’s “A New Dawn” holds the distinction of being the first Japanese animated feature directed by a first-time feature filmmaker to compete at the Berlin International Film Festival. After its Berlinale premiere, the film went on to win the Jury Award, given in Annecy’s Contrechamp section. The 76-minute feature is built around a distinctive green palette inspired by ‘Paris Green,’ a pigment once outlawed for its toxicity. Shinomiya, who earlier worked on Shinkai Makoto’s “Your Name.” (2016) and created the poster art for “The Garden of Words” (2013), handled the story, screenplay and direction on “A New Dawn,” in addition to its character design and art direction.

	The program closes with Paul Grimault’s “The King and the Mockingbird” (1952, 1980). Grimault finished an initial cut in 1952, which took a prize at the Venice Film Festival, but he later pulled the film from circulation, scrapped that version and spent decades reworking it into a new cut. Miyazaki Hayao paid tribute to it in his directorial debut, “Lupin III: The Castle of Cagliostro” (1979), and Studio Ghibli co-founder Takahata Isao once said he might never have gotten into animation had he not seen it. The film also numbers Bong Joon-ho among its admirers.

	BIFF festival director Jung Hanseok said, “Animation has recently become one of the most dynamic forms in global cinema, bridging East and West. That is why, for this year’s major Special Programs in Focus, we wanted to take a closer look at the world of Japanese animation, long one of the great traditions and powerhouses of the medium.”

	Jung said organizers set a handful of firm criteria for the lineup: the films needed, whenever feasible, to be original works made for theatrical release, and to represent either bold precedents from their era or a forward-looking vision for the medium, with preference given to titles that have seldom, if at all, played Korean cinemas. He added that the program deliberately left out Miyazaki Hayao and Takahata Isao, choosing instead works that had shaped both directors’ own filmmaking.
	

	“Some films can only be fully experienced in a theater. I hope audiences in Busan will not miss this rare opportunity to experience these works on the big screen. I am also deeply honored to welcome Rintaro, a living legend of Japanese animation, and four directors representing its next generation to BIFF,” Jung added.

	The 31st Busan International Film Festival runs Oct. 6-15, with venues centered on the Busan Cinema Center. The 21st Asian Contents & Film Market takes place alongside it, from Oct. 10-13.

schema.headline: Rintaro Returns to Korea After 17 Years for Busan’s Japanese Animation Special

title: ‘Lanterns’ Stars Aaron Pierre, Jasmine Cephas Jones on John’s Backstory Episode and How Being Black Informs His Quest to Become Green Lantern: ‘Fear Is Instilled in Our Ancestry’
description:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for Season 1, Episode 3 of “Lanterns,” now streaming on HBO Max.

	From the series’ opening scene, “La
body:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for Season 1, Episode 3 of “Lanterns,” now streaming on HBO Max.

	From the series’ opening scene, “Lanterns” sets up John Stewart’s (Aaron Pierre) calling to one day step into his own as Green Lantern. But it’s not until Sunday’s episode that we learn just how long John has been preparing and training — at the direction of his parents — to one day take Hal Jordan’s (Kyle Chandler) title.
	

	“It was a gift to have the opportunity to explore each of these characters with such enormous depth,” Pierre tells Variety of filming Episode 3. “It’s not a given that you get to have this much experience with a character, and live this much with a character in your portrayal.”


	In the latest “Lanterns” episode, John is grilled about his difficult life choices by one of the Guardians (Laura Linney) to see whether he’s worthy of replacing Hal. It’s the moment John has been waiting for all his life — the moment he gets to prove exactly why he is worthy of the ring.

	“I know exactly why me,” John says at the beginning of the interview.

	The episode cuts back and forth between John’s tense interview and his upbringing, revealing how John was conditioned to be fearless from a young age. The flashbacks show how desperate his parents become after John Stewart, Sr. (J. Alphonse Nicholson) is tested by the Guardians in the middle of the night, ultimately failing to become Green Lantern because he shows fear. Investing in John’s future is how the family finds salvation.

	As the son of somebody who had real potential to become Green Lantern, both John’s father and Bernadette (Jasmine Cephas Jones), his mother, recognize that if they do everything in their power, John will be the perfect candidate. In order to test him during his childhood, his parents do everything from shooting an apple off his head to leaving him stranded in a dangerous part of town, forcing John to fend for himself. They also lie, and tell him that the Guardians are always watching over him through birds.
	

	Knowing how everything John has done in his life has been with the goal of one day becoming Green Lantern, including joining the Marines and isolating himself from other people in his life, informed how Pierre played his budding dynamic with Chandler from the beginning.

	“He’s had a wealth of life experience, more life experience than people twice, three times his age have even come close,” Pierre says.

	Jones wanted to show that despite her stern attitude with John and forcing him to grow up, her love for her child always comes through.

	“I really wanted to show that militant side of her, and that she made that decision at a very young age for him, and that is his destiny,” Jones says. “No matter what happens, she’s gonna stick with it.”

	The biggest challenge was showing those moments of vulnerability when her character doesn’t speak, Jones says: “Like telling him to shoot a gun off of his father’s head, but then seeing in her face how much that breaks her.”

	When a young John learns that his parents lied to him about the Guardians always watching over him, he grapples with the reality that he wasn’t chosen, and will have to work harder than most people around him to prove that he’s worthy. At one point, Bernadette even tells him: “Sometimes, a Black man has to raise his own hand. Doesn’t mean you’re not good enough, doesn’t mean you’re not better. It just means they don’t see us.”

	“The importance of having no fear in a society, and also being a person of color in this country, fear is instilled in our ancestry as well,” Jones says. “That was also an important piece to talk about. How do we extract that for him to become the Green Lantern?”

	Nicholson adds: “It’s real, man. Yeah, I know we all want to escape from it but sometimes those questions need to be addressed even in our fictional worlds, right? Why do they make us have these feelings or why do they exist? And so just asking the questions sometimes allows room for people to talk about it. I think that’s what great writers do.” 

	The idea of raising John to be the next Green Lantern is largely born out of his father’s trauma. Investing in his son, and doing everything he can to give John the highest odds possible, becomes the only way he knows how to move forward.
	

	“He doesn’t want to let his son down. Essentially, he felt like he let himself down, he let his community down, let his wife down, so now it’s up to him to make sure that his son doesn’t feel that way and doesn’t go into the same spiral of depression,” Nicholson says. “It’s really cool to see him protect his son in a really tough way, but it’s tough love.”

	The major turning point in the episode comes when John takes matters into his own hands by shooting an apple off his mother’s head. He’s finally become exactly who his parents raised him to be.

	“It’s him taking a step into his own lane and really showing how fearless he is because that’s a huge risk, right?” Nicholson says. “He showed an immense amount of confidence, and I’m proud as his father to have shown him how to have that confidence early on.”

	As Pierre looks back on filming, one of the most enjoyable parts of the episode was getting to work with the child actors, including Jayce Eiland and Cairo Cash Lee, who play the younger versions of John.

	“They really need to be celebrated, acknowledged and commended for delivering all of the emotion and beyond that was necessary,” Pierre says. “It was very rare that we were working on the same location or on the same day because it’s a completely different timeline, but anytime I had the opportunity, I would definitely give them a fist and just tell them how proud I was.”

schema.headline: ‘Lanterns’ Stars Aaron Pierre, Jasmine Cephas Jones on John’s Backstory Episode and How Being Black Informs His Quest to Become Green Lantern: ‘Fear Is Instilled in Our Ancestry’

title: ‘Pokémon: Wild Card’ Movie Sets 2027 Release Date, Drops Anime Teaser Starring Trading Card Game Player
description:
It’s time to catch ’em all because Pokémon is heading back to the big screen.

	The popular trading card and video game franchise is returning with
body:
It’s time to catch ’em all because Pokémon is heading back to the big screen.

	The popular trading card and video game franchise is returning with “Pokémon: Wild Card,” a new movie releasing worldwide in 2027. The film was announced during the closing ceremony of the 2026 Pokémon World Championships, held in San Francisco. A short teaser also gave a brief look at the upcoming movie, which stars a trading card game player and a ghostly Pokémon named Mimikyu.
	

	The mysterious teaser reveals the trading card game player, who’s dressed in a yellow hoodie like Mimikyu. The ghost and fairy type Pokémon was introduced in “Sun” and “Moon,” the seventh generation games in the “Pokémon” franchise. It crudely disguises itself as a Pikachu, the mascot of the “Pokémon” series, but its true form is hidden below the yellow rag that it wears.




	

	



	Katsuhiko Kitada, who previously worked on anime films and shows like “The First Slam Dunk,” “Attack on Titan,” “Naruto: Shippuden” and more, will direct “Pokémon: Wild Card.” Character design is being handled by Akemi Hayashi, who has worked on “Banana Fish,” “Lazarus” and other anime. CloverWorks, the Japanese animation studio behind titles like “Spy X Family,” “Bocchi the Rock” and others, will produce the film.

	“Wild Card” is the first “Pokémon” movie made since 2020’s “Pokémon the Movie: Secrets of the Jungle,” which was released theatrically in Japan and worldwide on Netflix in 2021. The last “Pokémon” film to hit theaters worldwide was 2018’s “Pokémon the Movie: The Power of Us,” which received a limited release by Fathom Events outside of Japan.
	

	Next year will also see the release of “Winds” and “Waves,” the 10th generation of “Pokémon” titles. The franchise celebrated its 30th anniversary in 2026.

	Watch the teaser below.

schema.headline: ‘Pokémon: Wild Card’ Movie Sets 2027 Release Date, Drops Anime Teaser Starring Trading Card Game Player

title: NBCUniversal, U-Next Ink Sweeping Japan Partnership Spanning Streaming and Theme Parks
description: NBCUniversal and U-Next have entered into a long-term strategic partnership in Japan, bringing NBCUniversal’s international streaming brand Universa
body:
NBCUniversal and U-Next have entered into a long-term strategic partnership in Japan, bringing NBCUniversal’s international streaming brand Universal+ exclusively to the platform alongside joint initiatives with Universal Studios Japan and new global distribution pathways for Japanese content.

	U-Next, operated by Usen & U-Next Group, is Japan’s second-largest subscription video-on-demand platform behind Netflix, with more than 5.2 million paid subscribers as of May 2026, according to GEM Partners. The service combines movies, television series, anime, sports including the Premier League, live music and e-books in a single app.
	

	As the entertainment industry moves beyond standalone broadcasting, film and streaming segments toward a model centered on IP that spans digital platforms, live experiences and global distribution, the two companies aim to establish what they call a next-generation entertainment model in Japan.


	The partnership’s first pillar centers on Universal+, which will roll out in Japan starting in October 2026 as an exclusive offering on U-Next. The service will carry NBCUniversal’s catalog from studios including Universal Pictures, Focus Features, DreamWorks Animation, Illumination, Universal Studio Group and Sky, featuring franchises such as “The Super Mario Bros. Movie,” “Minions,” “Jurassic Park” and “Fast & Furious.” Beginning in the spring of 2027, U-Next will also offer major theatrical releases shortly after their cinema runs and first-run series from NBCUniversal on a rolling, exclusive basis.

	NBCUniversal’s 2026 theatrical slate will include event films such as Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” opening in Japan on Sept. 11, and Steven Spielberg’s “Disclosure Day,” opening Oct. 1. On the television side, the studio’s slate includes “The Five Star Weekend,” scripted series “Line of Fire” and “War,” along with library titles “Suits” and “Heroes.”
	

	The second pillar centers on live experiences tied to Universal Studios Japan (USJ), which marks its 25th anniversary in 2026. U-Next and USJ will explore joint development of live music events, exclusive experiences and benefits for U-Next’s subscriber base, and the planning and production of video content featuring the park.

	The third pillar will build new distribution pathways for Japanese dramas, anime, films and U-Next original productions through NBCUniversal’s Peacock service in the U.S. and Universal+ in Latin America, with the companies aiming to expand into additional markets over time.

	“What sets apart this multi-faceted partnership is the innovative breadth achieved for both businesses,” said Chris Taylor, managing director, Asia Pacific, TV distribution and international networks and direct-to-consumer for NBCUniversal. “For NBCUniversal, it brings together our film and television catalog, our theme park experiences through Universal Studios Japan and our global distribution network – all under one roof for Japanese audiences.”

	“U-Next’s impressive performance, having recently eclipsed five million subscribers, make them an ideal platform for NBCUniversal to align with on this ambitious partnership that includes the first fully-loaded Universal+ launch in Asia Pacific – reinforcing the importance of the Japanese market to our overall business,” Taylor said. He added that the collaboration builds on NBCUniversal’s strategy of pairing premium branded entertainment destinations with its traditional licensing business, and that the companies see an opportunity to extend the reach of U-Next’s Japanese dramas and anime as Asian content grows in global popularity.

	“We are very pleased to enter into this strategic partnership with NBCUniversal,” said Tsutsumi Tenshin, president and representative director of U-Next Co., Ltd. “While continuing to build on the service and trust we have cultivated to date, we aim to evolve U-Next beyond a service for simply watching video content into a platform where people can discover entertainment, become passionate about it, connect with real-world experiences, and bring Japanese content to audiences around the world.”

	“This partnership is the first step toward realizing those possibilities,” Tsutsumi added. “Together, we will build a new kind of entertainment service that extends beyond streaming.”
	

	Specific initiatives under the partnership, including further USJ collaborations, the NBCUniversal content lineup, global expansion plans for Japanese content, user campaigns and new live event projects, will be unveiled on a rolling basis starting this fall.

title: Helsinki’s Finnish Film Affair Unveils Film, Series Pitches and Panels, Strikes First Nordic Genre Lab Partnership (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Finland’s biggest international film and TV drama market, Finnish Film Affair, unspooling parallel to the Helsinki Intl. Film Festival – Love & Anar
body:
Finland’s biggest international film and TV drama market, Finnish Film Affair, unspooling parallel to the Helsinki Intl. Film Festival – Love & Anarchy, has unpacked its full program, rolling out Sept. 23-25 in the Finnish capital.

	In the pure Nordic tradition of mind-blowing chills and thrills, genre-bending content and documentaries are headlining the slate of 38 titles from the Nordics and beyond, to be pitched to 500-plus attendees at FFA’s centerpiece Showcase Day, Sept. 24.
	

	Selected as FFA opener, Hanna Bergholm’s horror “Nightborn,” top winner at the Fantasia Festival and Berlinale Golden Bear contender, will set the tone for this year’s Nordic market, where eight Nordic genre pics in development will compete for best pitch, as part of a new partnership with the Nordic Genre Lab. The training and networking program is the brainchild of seasoned Finnish executive Laura Laaksonen (Purr PR), co-founder of Nordic Genre Lab with former Netflix executive Claire Willats (Two Magpie Entertainment).




	

					Lydia Taylerson
									Courtesy of Alejandro Ramirez
	



	“We’ve partly replaced our Finnish Weird section with the Nordic Genre Lab showcase which fills the need on the market for fun, quality, genre-bending content from the Nordics,” FFA head of industry Lydia Taylerson told Variety.

	Genre projects to watch include Making Movies’ “Alma” helmed by Pete Riski (“Icebreaker,” “Dark Floors”) from a script by Ilja Rautsi (“Red Snow,” “Nightborn”), the first Faroese horror feature “Whistler,” produced by Outlier Projects, “Linden Lane 6,” produced by the prolific banner It’s Alive Films (“Euthanizer,” “100 Litres of Gold”) and “Trespassers,” produced by Patrick Andersson (“Midsommar”), with Mylla Films co-founder Jakob Abrahamsson.
	

	Headlining the six-title documentary slate selected by Tayleron, Mourad-Anis Moussa (Visions du Réel) and Erika Dilday (American Documentary Inc.) is “Lonesome Land,” by prominent filmmaker Virpi Suutari.



	

					“Lonesome Land”
									Courtesy of Euphoria Film
	



	Besides Suutari’s latest plea to safeguard Finnish forests after her multi-awarded “Once Upon a Time in a Forest,” topics range from a tribute to working-class Italian men during WW2 in “Umarells – We Know Better,” to biopics about New York/Helsinki-based late artist Iria Leino in “Dear Iria,” and fallen-from grace Olympic medallist Mika Myllylä in “Myllylä.”

	On the scripted front, the eight films in development and five works in progress selected by Taylerson, Katre Kajamäe-Gupta (Eurimages) and Natasha Degnova (LeveK) play across an equally wide range of topics and genres.

	“We have familiar faces such as Aku Louhimies, Pamela Tola, the up-and-coming Laura Hyppönen, who first pitched her project “Lex Julia” at Finnish Film Affair in 2021, and true newcomers Kyran Davies and Scott Quinn with “The Lost Sons of Nada,” one of the rare Finnish-U.K. co-production projects,” noted Taylerson.

	“Lex Julia” is also one of four Nordic selections, together with the Norwegian thriller “11 Hours,” the Danish psycho drama “Without You” and Icelandic coming-of-age “Just a Kid.”

	As for the popular Series session curated by APFI (Audiovisual Producers Finland), this year’s slate of six TV titles range from thrillers and crime shows to teen drama and animation from hot helmers including American Film Institute graduate Jojo Erholtz (“Maria Kallio,” “Tape”) and Elin Grönblom (“Bloodsuckers”).

	European Drive“All in all, it’s been very interesting to receive a record number of submissions for the Fiction in Development (45), Fiction in Progress (11-the largest number since 2022) and Documentaries (22), which proves the attractiveness of Finland as filming and production destination,” Taylerson observed.

	“Also, this year we ended up with quite a few European co-productions in the final lineup, another display of the growing trend of Europe-leaning partnerships,” she said, underscoring the endemic lack of public funding for film in Finland, forcing indie producers to look beyond national borders for coin.
	

	“Finns have to continue widening their networking opportunities across Europe, which is why we’ve signed a new collaboration with the Marché du Film for the inaugural Producers Network Award,” she added.

	To help Nordic producers and filmmakers further hone their skills, more than 20 top industry experts, such as Isabel Arrate Fernandez (IDFA), Jason Gutierrez (Tribeca), Hugo Rosak (Karlovy Vary), Jim Kolmar (SXSW), Celine Dornier (IPR.VC), James Copp (Night Train Media), Mette Damgaard-Sørensen (Danish Film Institute) and Kjetil Omberg (Norwegian Film Institute), will take center stage to discuss among other things how to better budget, finance a feature, co-produce, navigate the international festivals, distribution landscape and the next Agora EU program in Europe.

	The two-day panel sessions will close Sept. 25 with the popular XYZ masterclass, sponsored by U.S. genre specialists XYZ Films, FFA and Film Tampere, which will zoom in on how the Norwegian action comedy “The Trip” morphed into the U.S. remake “Over Your Dead Body,” shot in Tampere. XYZ Films founder Aram Tertzakian, producer of the U.S. version starring Jason Segel and Samara Weaving, will moderate the talk.

	Furthermore, as part of the FFA training scheme Nordic Flair, 10 Nordic producers with a first feature project, will have access to the full FFA program and micro-sessions with mentors Max Malka (Banijay Finland), Jim Kolmar (SXSW), Gary Cranner (Mantra Films Norway) and Natascha Degnova (LevelK).

	“We have amazing guests, with impressive resumes. It makes sense to tap into their expertise and insight and help Nordic professionals take their first step into the industry,” added Taylerson.



	

					“Halima”
									Courtesy of Keke Leppala
	



	Full list of FFA projects:Fiction in Development:“Babyface,” directed by Aleksi Delikouras, produced by Helsinkifilmi (Finland)“Big Deal,” directed by Hedda Mjøen, produced by Kruela Film (Norway, Finland, Estonia)“Kekri: Trick or Die,” directed by Jari Pauna, produced by Pari Pauna Pictures (Finland)“The Big Party,” directed by Nicole Genovese, produced by Yukundun, Frakas, Good Hand (France, Belgium, Finland)“The Bottom Line,” directed by Jon Blåhed, produced by Just Republic, Anagram Sweden (Finland, Sweden)“The Lost Sons of Nada,” directed by Kyran Davies, Scott Quinn, produced by Poolboy, Falcon Nest Films (Finland, U.K.)“The Weight of a Man,” directed by Jojo Erholtz, produced by Whatever Pictures (Finland)“Tick Fever,” directed by Sebastian Granskog, produced by Characterhouse (Finland)
	

	Fiction in Progress“Good Times, “directed by Pamela Tola, produced by Bardy Studios, Estar (Finland, Estonia)“Halima,” directed by Naima Mohamud, produced by It’s Alive Films, No-Office Films, Vico Films (Finland, Ireland)“Lapland War,” directed by Aku Louhimies, produced by Backmann & Hoderoff (Finland)“Lex Julia,” directed by Laura Hyppönen, produced by Greenlight Productions, Orka Film, Alexandra Film, Götafilm, Breidablick (Finland, Poland, Estonia, Sweden) – also part of the Nordic Selection“The Campers,” directed by Kari Ketonen, produced by Red Carpet Film & TV (Finland)

	Nordic Genre Lab“Alma,” directed by Pete Riski, produced by Making Movies (Finland)“Echo Chamber,” directed by Juha Fiilin, produced by Fiilin Good Films (Finland)“Linden Lane 6,” directed by Josefina Rautiainen, produced by It’s Alive Films (Finland)“Long Way Home,” directed by Kjersti Helen Rasmussen, produced by Truewest (Norway)“Sauna Diplomacy,” directed by Teemu Niukkanen, produced by TACK Films (Finland)“The Evil Eye,” directed by Kristian Lidegaard, produced by Manna Film (Denmark)“Trespassers,” directed by Johannes Persson, produced by Mylla Films (Sweden)“Whistler,” directed by Gudmund Helmsdal, produced by Outlier Projects (Faroe Islands)

	Nordic Selection“11 Hours,” directed by Daniel Fahre, produced by Fenomen Studios, Maha Film (Norway)“Just a Kid,” directed by Vala Ómarsdóttir, produced by Ursus Parvus (Iceland)“Without You,” directed by Nils Holst-Jensen, produced by Hyæne Film (Denmark)

	Documentaries“Umarell – We Know Better,” directed by Hannu-Pekka Vitikainen, produced by Zone2 Pictures (Finland, Germany)“P,” directed by Vadimir Loginov, produced by Korraks Film (Estonia)“Lonesome Land,” directed by Virpi Suutari, produced by Euphoria Film, Tambo Film (Finland, Denmark)“Darkness Counts,” directed by Anna Antsalo, produced by Ekokuvayhtiö Viisi (Finland)“Unicorns Never Die,” directed by Janne Tanskanen, Olli Vuokko, produced by Kinocompany (Finland)“Dear Iria,” directed by Janna Kyllästinen, produced by Iria the Film, BUFO (USA, Finland)“Marianne’s Lament,” directed by Antti Haase, Pariana Reyes, produced by Making Movies (Finland, Bulgaria, Mexico, TBA)“Myllylä,” directed by Sean Ricks, Jussi Sandhu, Ville Hakonen, produced by Wacky Tie Films, Story AB, f(x) Produksjoner (Finland, Sweden, Norway)
	

	Series“Checkmate,” written by Veli-Pekka Hänninen, produced by Solar Films (Finland)“The Crimes of Others,” written by Sami Keski-Vähälä, Tara Kylmä, produced by Funfar Studios (Finland)“Body in the Closet,” written/directed by Elin Grönblom, co-written by Josefin Sonck, produced by Warner Bros Int’l Television Production (Finland)“Tango Metal,” directed by Jojo Erholtz, written by Mia Ylönen, Tua Harno, produced by Helsinki-filmi, Glassriver (Finland, Iceland)“Arctic Divers,” directed/written by Laura Satimus, co-written by Petro Salminen, produced by Kopla Entertainment, Yle Asia (Finland)“The Tradewife Theory,” written by Vilja Kesmimäki, produced by Just Republic (Finland)

title: Pink Floyd’s Roger Waters Boards Palestinian Art and Resistance Documentary ‘Freedom Theatre’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Singer-songwriter and Pink Floyd co-founder Roger Waters has signed on as executive producer on filmmaker Rishi Pelham’s debut feature documentary,
body:
Singer-songwriter and Pink Floyd co-founder Roger Waters has signed on as executive producer on filmmaker Rishi Pelham’s debut feature documentary, “Freedom Theatre.”

	Described as “an immersive and sensory character study,” the film follows resistance fighter turned artist Ahmed Tobasi into the creative heart of the Jenin refugee camp in Palestine, where he fights to keep his theater open amidst imminent destruction.




	

									Courtesy of Rishi Pelham/Bathtub Films
	



	“I didn’t intentionally set out to make this film,” Pelham said. “I kept returning to Jenin, to the theater, to the camp, and over time the story insisted on being told. What drew me in was the tension between two worlds: the black-box rehearsal room, sealed and controllable, and the camp outside, alive, volatile, and impossible to contain. Slowly, these spaces began to bleed into one another.”
	

	Pelham also co-composed the documentary’s original score, which features prominent Palestinian artists such as techno DJ and producer Sama’ Abdulhadi.

	Shot over the course of five years, “Freedom Theatre” is currently in the final stages of post-production.

	Suzanne Harb is producing the documentary in collaboration with Pelham for London-based Bathtub Films, behind the director’s award-winning 2019 drama “Hilda” that was executive produced by Tim Roth.

	Also on board “Freedom Theatre” are executive partners Khaled Habayeb and Alaa Alasad of Amman-based Tabi360, whose credits include Zain Duraie’s acclaimed family drama “Sink,” which premiered last year in Toronto, and Ameer Fakher Eldin’s 2025 Berlin competition title “Yunan.”
	

	In Waters, the project has gained a prominent activist and supporter of Palestinian liberation. He is among the hundreds of artists who recently signed an open letter calling for the Venice Film Festival “to take concrete action in support of Palestine.”

	The film team is planning a festival circuit rollout and will be attending the Venice fest for meetings with potential partners.

title: Dolly Parton's Niece Misses Her 4 AM Calls After Death
description:
Dolly Parton's Niece
                          I'd Do Anything for One More 4 AM Call
body:
Dolly Parton's Niece
                          I'd Do Anything for One More 4 AM Call
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Dolly Parton's niece says one of the things she'll miss most about the country legend is getting calls from her at 4 AM.
      
    
            Lainey Parton shared an emotional tribute to Instagram after Dolly was laid to rest ... saying it still doesn't feel real she's gone and she'd give anything to see her name pop up on her phone again.
      
    
    
              
                
  
    
            Lainey wrote ... "I'm even going to miss those 4 AM calls."
      

            She also opened up about how close they were, saying Dolly -- who never had children of her own -- made her nieces and nephews feel like they were hers.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Growing up, Dolly always made Lainey feel like she was enough and never made her dreams seem too big.
      
    
            And that support went beyond words ... Dolly financially supported her through beauty school and helped get her career started.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            She also recalled being a nervous freshman in high school when Dolly asked her to sing on her "Smoky Mountain DNA" album ... saying Dolly made her feel safe, confident and like she belonged beside her.
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported ... Dolly's loved ones gathered Friday at her Nashville burial site alongside her late husband, Carl Dean.
      
    
            Lainey closed the tribute simply ... "I love you, Granny. Always."

title: Brandi Glanville Talks Kim Zolciak Son Case, Admits She's a Hypocrite
description:
Brandi Glanville
                          Kim Zolciak's Son Case Hits Different as a Boy Mom
body:
Brandi Glanville
                          Kim Zolciak's Son Case Hits Different as a Boy Mom
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 30, 2026
                            5:15 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Brandi Glanville knows she's wading into dangerous territory talking about Kim Zolciak's 15-year-old son ... and she's admitting she's being a hypocrite for doing it.
      
    
            Brandi addressed the allegations against Kroy "KJ" Biermann Jr. on her "Brandi Glanville Unfiltered" podcast ... saying she normally believes underage kids shouldn't be dragged into the spotlight just because their parents put them on TV.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            But she says this case struck a nerve because she's a mom of boys.
      

            Brandi said she drilled consent into her sons growing up ... telling them they couldn't even hold hands, kiss or hug a girl without asking first.
      
    
            She also acknowledged the irony of discussing KJ publicly, saying ... "I'm realizing I'm a hypocrite, because I'm saying we shouldn't talk about kids that are underage, but I'm sitting here talking about it."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported ... KJ was arrested earlier this month and charged with aggravated sodomy and aggravated sexual battery after a female classmate accused him of sexually assaulting her inside a gym changing area.
      
    
            Kim has vehemently denied the allegations on her son's behalf, telling TMZ he "categorically denies" the alleged conduct and claiming he passed a polygraph examination.
      
    
            KJ remains jailed without bond.
